result.title: Testing Flexible Start Times at Work
result.objective: Learners will understand and correctly use phase in and take effect in workplace contexts.

exercises.prompt: In sentence 2, 'Managers plan to phase in the change over six weeks,' what does 'phase in' mean here?

options.text: It means they will introduce the change gradually in stages over six weeks.
options.explanation: Correct: this matches gradual introduction in stages over six weeks.

options.text: It means they will cancel the change completely before six weeks end.
options.explanation: Incorrect: cancel is the opposite of introducing a change gradually.

options.text: It means they will announce the change suddenly without any preparation.
options.explanation: Incorrect: suddenly contradicts the idea of doing something gradually in stages.

exercises.explanation: The six-week period for reporting problems shows gradual introduction.

exercises.prompt: Choose the sentence that uses 'phase in' correctly and naturally.

options.text: The school will phases in the new timetable over three weeks.
options.explanation: Incorrect: change phases to phase after will.

options.text: The school will phase in the new timetable over three weeks.
options.explanation: Correct: this uses the verb phrase with correct grammar and natural word order.

options.text: The school will phase in the new timetable over three weeks ago.
options.explanation: Incorrect: remove ago because will refers to the future.

exercises.explanation: Only one option uses phase in with correct grammar and natural timing.

exercises.prompt: In sentence 3, 'The new schedule will take effect on 1 December,' what does 'take effect' mean here?

options.text: It means the schedule will be discussed as a possible idea on that date.
options.explanation: Incorrect: discussing an idea is different from starting to apply it.

options.text: It means the schedule will be cancelled and stop working on that date.
options.explanation: Incorrect: cancelled means ending while the context shows starting to apply.

options.text: It means the schedule will start to apply and become official on that date.
options.explanation: Correct: this matches starting to apply after the trial and review.

exercises.explanation: The context after trial and review shows the schedule becomes official.

exercises.prompt: Choose the sentence that uses 'take effect' correctly and naturally.

options.text: The new safety rules will take effect next Monday.
options.explanation: Correct: this uses the fixed phrase with correct grammar and natural timing.

options.text: The new safety rules will take an effect next Monday.
options.explanation: Incorrect: remove an because the fixed collocation is take effect.

options.text: The new safety rules will takes effect next Monday.
options.explanation: Incorrect: change takes to take after will.

exercises.explanation: Only one option keeps the fixed phrase take effect with correct grammar.

exercises.prompt: Imagine you are an organizer of a weekend sports club. Write a short message to members explaining that you will introduce a new online booking system gradually. Write 2-3 sentences and use the phrase phase in.
exercises.sampleAnswer: We will phase in our new online booking system over the next two weeks. Please keep using the old form until your group is notified.
selfCheck: I wrote 2-3 sentences as a club message to members.
I used the phrase phase in correctly for gradual introduction.
My message explains the new system and what members should do.
exercises.explanation: Compare with the model and self-assess; no automatic grade.
